current-planning.caption: Today: the planning screen at main d7f3006, captured with npm run e2e:capture (desktop Chromium).
current-planning.alt: Current planning screen with the parchment map of Spain, faction washes, counters, and the in-map orders pane.

current-resolution.caption: Today: the turn results screen with battle cards.
current-resolution.alt: Current resolution screen with the turn report.

setup-timer.caption: Mockup (idea 3): a Turn timer setting on the setup screen and a countdown beside End Turn. Values are illustrative; the research recommends Off, 1, 5, 10 min now, with 30 min and 1 h shown as online-only.
setup-timer.alt: Setup screen with a Turn timer select and a countdown chip.

planning-resources.caption: Mockup (ideas 1 and 2): a resource bar (Funds, Manpower, optional Materiel), a Recruit menu with cost, training turns and site, and Replenish on a depleted regiment. Numbers are illustrative and untuned.
planning-resources.alt: Planning pane with a resource bar and a recruit menu.

city-build.caption: Mockup (idea 4): a city panel with garrison, yields, and build options. The research recommends four buildings (Depot, Workshop, Fortifications, Port); the mockup's fact sheet also shows an AA battery and rail depot as later options.
city-build.alt: City panel for a major city with yields and build options.

partition-map.caption: Mockup (idea 7): Andalucia split into its eight provinces with faction washes, drawn schematically over the real map; province shapes are hand-drawn. The pane says moves count province to province, which is the deferred option: the research recommends that moves and battles stay on territories for now.
partition-map.alt: Andalucia divided into eight schematic provinces with faction colours.

rail-lane.caption: Mockup (idea 5): rail lines drawn as hatched track with a capacity badge and a rail move arrow distinct from road moves. Capacities are illustrative.
rail-lane.alt: Map with hatched rail lines, a capacity badge, and a rail move arrow.

unit-counters.caption: Mockup (idea 8): today's counters beside proposed new types in each faction colour. The research recommends adding artillery now and deferring tanks, cavalry, and AA; aircraft become abstract wings rather than counters.
unit-counters.alt: Sheet of NATO-style counters for existing and proposed unit types.

general-chip.caption: Mockup (idea 8): a commander chip on a stack, shown as initials in a medallion. The mockup shows a +1 roll effect; the research recommends display-only chips, with no rules effect. Miaja is shown at Madrid on turn 1; historically he took command there in November 1936.
general-chip.alt: Counter stack with a commander medallion chip and an info card.

d20-battle-card.caption: Mockup (idea 9): today's battle card extended with a d20 roll, modifiers, and a graded result ladder showing where the result landed. Numbers are illustrative. The research's ladder works differently: score = roll + 3 x odds column, with today's modifiers tripled (dug in at +3 becomes +9). The mockup shows a plain 1 to 20 row.
d20-battle-card.alt: Battle card with a d20 roll breakdown and a graded outcome ladder.

weather-badge.caption: Mockup (idea 12): a weather badge in the planning header and a per-zone forecast with effects. Effects shown are illustrative; the research recommends a soft set (Mud -1, Snow -1, Severe cold -2, no digging in during snow or cold). Turn 11 is 18 to 31 December 1936 under two-week turns from 31 July.
weather-badge.alt: Planning header with a weather badge and a forecast panel.

movement-exhaustion.caption: Mockup (idea 6): fatigue pips and a movement allowance on a planned multi-step route. The research recommends one move per turn with exhaustion through morale, so the movement readout illustrates the deferred option.
movement-exhaustion.alt: Counters with fatigue pips on a multi-step route.

harness-report.caption: Mockup (idea 11): example output of a proposed npm run sim command and its HTML summary. Numbers are based on today's soak and are labelled as example output.
harness-report.alt: Terminal output and a summary card with win shares and intervals.
